verdict.line: You lose if you stand in extended auto-trades where his Q (Knuckle Down) and passive regen outlast you; you win if you poke with Q (Snip Snip!) and R (Needlework) from range and force him to walk into Hallowed Mist to do anything.

brief.thesis: Sett's whole kit rewards prolonged melee exchanges — Q (Knuckle Down) empowers his next two autos off max health, his passive heals more the lower his health drops, and W (Haymaker) banks every point of damage he eats as Grit for a shield and true-damage punch. Gwen has none of that sustain; her kit is a hit-and-run cycle of Q poke and E (Skip 'n Slash) dash-ins, not a standing fight. The 46.4% head-to-head over 978 games reflects that Sett wins the fights Gwen's forced into, not the ones she chooses.

theirWindow.when: Facebreaker and Haymaker both off cooldown
theirWindow.what: Sett can land the E (Facebreaker, 16-10s cooldown, range 490) stun and dump a full Haymaker shield-punch in the same engage. Back out of his 490-range threat zone entirely rather than trading autos.

yourWindow.when: his E and W are both down from a recent trade
yourWindow.what: Step in with Q (Snip Snip!, 6.5-3.5s cooldown) for the true-damage center hit and passive proc, then E out. This is the only window where he can't punish the dash with a stun.

powerCurve.note: Q empowered autos win early trades outright
Facebreaker stun unlocks, Gwen still fragile
The Show Stopper adds a full all-in
shorter E cooldown lets Gwen kite

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: 86.2% pick rate at 45.3% win rate; the extra potion offsets how much poke damage you'll eat just walking up to land a Q.

boots.why: 57.7% pick rate at 47.2% win rate; Sett's damage is entirely physical (Q bonus autos, Haymaker's physical side-damage), so flat auto reduction blunts both his poke and his all-in.

core.why: First item in the highest-performing path (58.7% win rate, 223 games) and gives the early stat foundation to survive his level 3-8 all-in window.
Second in that same 58.7% win rate path; scales A Thousand Cuts and Q's true-damage hits against a target that's rarely at full health once he's using his passive regen to stay in the fight.
Completes the top-performing build path; by level 14+ this is what lets your Q and R burst outrace his sustain.

situational.when: he has The Show Stopper up and is grouping with his team to force a pick on you
the game goes long and lane trades keep extending past a single poke exchange
you need more attack speed to land extra A Thousand Cuts procs in prolonged skirmishes

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror's healing scales with the extended trades Sett tries to force; Bone Plating in Resolve is the more important piece here, since it blunts his Q's two empowered autos plus Facebreaker as one burst window.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport posts the best win rate of the three measured setups (47.9% over 11.9% pick); since the matchup favors Sett through level 8, Teleport lets you reset waves safely instead of forcing early fights you lose, and you scale into the levels where you're ahead.

playing.title: Poke, don't stand
playing.detail: Land Q (Snip Snip!) and retreat rather than holding position for a second cast; standing still is exactly the fight his Q and passive regen are built for.

playing.title: Track his Grit bar
playing.detail: W (Haymaker) banks every point of damage he's taken as Grit passively. If he's been soaking your Q pokes for a while, expect a shield plus true-damage punch — back off before he casts it.

playing.title: Dash in, dash out with E
playing.detail: E (Skip 'n Slash) dashes a short distance and grants attack speed, range, and magic damage on-hit; if it connects the cooldown partially refunds, so use it to re-engage immediately rather than committing to a stand-and-swing.

playing.title: Respect the 490-range stun
playing.detail: E (Facebreaker) pulls enemies on opposite sides of Sett for a stun, or a slow if only one side is hit; don't let minions or terrain put you on the far side of him in his range.

playing.title: Play around his R cooldown
playing.detail: The Show Stopper is 120s at rank 1, dropping to 80s at rank 3; after he uses it to displace and slam a target, you get a long window where his biggest engage tool is gone.

playing.title: Save R for free hits
playing.detail: Needlework can be cast up to two more times and applies your passive on each hit at 1200 range; use it to poke safely when his Facebreaker and Haymaker are both on cooldown instead of saving it purely for kill threat.

playing.title: Don't chase a whiffed all-in
playing.detail: His passive grants more regen the lower his health drops, so a missed Facebreaker or Haymaker isn't a free follow-up kill — disengage and let your next poke cycle do the work instead.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, boots, runes, summoners, and all win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning — why each trade pattern works — is my own read of the ability kits, not a measured stat.
